title: Finance (Income Taxes) Act 2026 (Act 23 of 2026) assented and published: Side-by-Side MTT exemption now law
summary: The Finance (Income Taxes) Act 2026 (No. 23 of 2026) was assented to by the President on 29 October 2026 and published in the Acts Supplement on 4 November 2026 (Gazette Acts Supplement No. 25, Friday 6 November 2026). This enacts the Bill passed on 6 October 2026. Part 2 amends the Multinational Enterprise (Minimum Tax) Act 2024: sections 38 and 49(b) — the Side-by-Side package provisions that exempt qualifying US-parented groups from Singapore's Multinational Enterprise Top-up Tax (IIR) while leaving Domestic Top-up Tax in place — are deemed to have come into operation on 1 January 2026. Other MMT amendments largely commence on 4 November 2026; sections 37, 39, 49(d) and 50 (including some regulation-making powers) commence on a date the Minister appoints by Gazette notification. Safe-harbour detail still depends on forthcoming MMT Regulations.

title: Inclusive Framework 18th Plenary reviews Global Minimum Tax implementation and Side-by-Side progress
summary: On 30 October 2026 the OECD published the outcome of the OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework’s 18th Plenary (Paris, 28–30 October 2026). Members reviewed Global Minimum Tax implementation, including the Side-by-Side package: an updated impact assessment, interaction with tax incentives, priorities for further simplification and guidance, progress on full legislative reviews, development of the GloBE co-ordination mechanism, and review of the two pre-existing regimes that timely requested Side-by-Side safe-harbour qualification. The statement notes that by 2027 GMT or Side-by-Side-eligible minimum tax regimes will cover close to 65 jurisdictions. No new model rules, rates or safe-harbour parameters were issued.

summary: IRAS updated its GloBE Rules and DTT page (last updated 13 October 2026) with a published list of Qualified Tax Incentives (QTIs) for the Substance-based Tax Incentive Safe Harbour under Singapore's Domestic Top-up Tax. title: Parliament passes the Finance (Income Taxes) Bill 2026: US-parented groups exempted from Singapore's MTT, DTT unchanged
summary: Second Minister for Finance Jeffrey Siow moved the second reading of Bill No. 22/2026 on 6 October 2026 and Parliament passed it the same day. Clauses 38 and 49(b) give effect to the Side-by-Side package: US multinational enterprises are exempted from Singapore's Multinational Enterprise Top-up Tax (IIR), while the Domestic Top-up Tax continues to apply to all MNEs in Singapore, including US groups. Under the Bill as tabled, those clauses are deemed to operate from 1 January 2026. Other clauses (36, 37, 39 to 50) align the MMT Act with further international updates, including exchange of GloBE Information Returns so groups only need to file the GIR in one jurisdiction. The Act still needs presidential assent and gazetting, and the detailed safe harbour rules are to follow in regulations.

title: Romania deposits instrument of ratification for the STTR Multilateral Convention (in force for Romania from 1 February 2027)
summary: On 2 October 2026 Romania deposited its instrument of ratification for the Multilateral Convention to Facilitate the Implementation of the Pillar Two Subject to Tax Rule (the STTR Convention). The Convention will enter into force for Romania on 1 February 2027. This follows Albania's 15 September 2026 ratification, which already triggered the Convention's general entry into force on 1 January 2027. The STTR remains a treaty-based rule on certain cross-border intragroup payments taxed below 9% in the recipient jurisdiction; no covered tax treaties are yet in practical effect solely from this deposit.

title: Inclusive Framework releases September 2026 Administrative Guidance (Explicitly Conditional Taxes; QDMTT local accounts with mismatched periods)
summary: New Administrative Guidance says an 'Explicitly Conditional Tax' (one that only bites when a Qualified IIR/UTPR applies, or switches off under the Side-by-Side Safe Harbour) is not a Covered Tax, and a DMTT with that feature cannot be a QDMTT. It also clarifies that a QDMTT can still use local financial accounting standards for the QDMTT Safe Harbour where a local entity's accounting period differs from the UPE's year, provided the same period is used for that entity in the consolidated accounts. The document was approved by the Inclusive Framework on 2 September 2026 and published on 11 September 2026.
